verdict: Target's sales rose 5.3% to $26.5B and profit doubled to $1.9B — but $994M of that came from one-off tariff refunds; even without them, EPS rose a solid 20%.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: net sales of $26.5B vs $25.2B a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: includes $1.65 from tariff refunds; up 20% excluding them

kpis.label: Comparable sales
kpis.note: traffic up 3.6%; digital comparable sales up 8.7%

kpis.label: Tariff refunds
kpis.note: one-off IEEPA refunds booked as a reduction in cost of sales

segments.name: Food & beverage
segments.note: Groceries — Target's biggest category, and it grew at a high single-digit rate.

segments.name: Apparel & accessories
segments.note: Clothing and accessories — essentially flat vs a year ago.

segments.name: Hardlines (Fun 101)
segments.note: Toys, electronics and seasonal 'Fun 101' goods — the fastest-growing big category, up double digits.

segments.name: Home furnishings & décor
segments.note: Furniture and home décor — essentially flat.

segments.name: Beauty
segments.note: Beauty and personal care, including the Ulta shop-in-shop format.

segments.name: Other & non-merchandise
segments.note: Other merchandise ($48M) plus money that is not store sales at all: Roundel advertising ($279M), credit-card profit sharing ($139M) and other income ($174M) — up over 20%.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Selling, general and administrative — store payroll, marketing and running the company.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of stores, fixtures and technology over their useful lives (excluding depreciation already counted in cost of sales).

otherDetail: Net interest expense of $98M plus $3M of net other expense — a $101M cost below the operating line.
oneTimers: $994M of IEEPA tariff refunds received in the quarter were booked as a reduction of cost of sales, adding $752M to net earnings and $1.65 to EPS. Excluding the refunds, EPS rose 20% YoY and gross margin was about 29.9% instead of the reported 33.7%.
footerNote: Target had not yet reported Q3 FY26 as of November 7, 2026 (that quarter ended October 31, 2026), so this page covers its latest reported quarter, Q2 FY26.

takeaways.title: Shoppers came back
takeaways.text: Comparable sales rose 3.8% on 3.6% more traffic, with growth in all six core categories. Digital comparable sales rose 8.7%, led by same-day delivery up more than 25%.

takeaways.title: Refunds flatter the margin
takeaways.text: Gross margin was 33.7% vs 29.0% a year ago — but $994M of one-off tariff refunds sit inside it. Without them the margin was about 29.9%, still an improvement.

takeaways.title: Profit doubled — honestly, mostly the refund
takeaways.text: EPS doubled to $4.11 from $2.05. Strip out the $1.65 refund benefit and EPS still rose 20%, which is the cleaner read on the quarter.
